links.outcome: Expert-rated completeness and accuracy of ChatGPT-4 vs PICU specialist answers on factual and reasoning questions
links.effect: ChatGPT-4 preferred in 60% of factual comparisons (p<0.001) and more complete (p=0.02); specialist preferred in 67% of clinical reasoning comparisons, ChatGPT-4 less accurate (p<0.0001).
links.quote: ChatGPT-4 demonstrated superior completeness in factual knowledge (p = 0.02) but lower accuracy in clinical reasoning (p < 0.0001).

links.outcome: Blinded expert preference between ChatGPT-4 and PICU specialist answers to same questions
links.effect: ChatGPT-4 preferred in 60% of factual knowledge comparisons (p<0.001); specialist preferred in 67% of clinical reasoning comparisons (p<0.0001); integration of both favoured in 37%.
links.quote: ChatGPT-4 was preferred in 60% of factual knowledge comparisons (p < 0.001), while the PICU specialist's responses were preferred in 67% of clinical reasoning comparisons (p < 0.0001).

screen.reason: The study compares ChatGPT-4 responses to human specialist responses on paediatric intensive care medical education questions, evaluating baseline accuracy and completeness rather than testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
